name: Italy
summary: EU citizens only register. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can use the investor visa (from EUR 250,000 in a start-up), the elective residence visa (about EUR 31,000 a year of passive income, no work) or, since March 2026, a digital nomad visa (about EUR 28,000 a year).
naturalisation: 10 years of legal residence for most non-EU nationals (4 for EU citizens per general knowledge), with Italian language (B1, general knowledge) and integration requirements; the investor visa does not shorten it. Citizenship by descent was tightened by Decree-Law 36/2025 (converted into Law 74/2025).
dual_citizenship_note: A foreigner naturalising in Italy is not required to renounce their other nationality (Law 91/1992 art. 11), though their home country may require it.

routes.tax_note: Tax residence: more than 183 days or registration in the population register. EU citizens' naturalisation in 4 years is from general knowledge (Law 91/1992 art. 9), not re-sourced.
routes.name: EU free movement (anagrafe registration)
routes.summary: EU citizens register with the municipality after 3 months; permanent residence after 5 years.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport; worker, self-employed or economically inactive with resources and health cover. Permanent right after 5 years of continuous legal residence (Directive 2004/38).

routes.investment_options: Italian company equity EUR 500,000; philanthropic donation EUR 1,000,000 (non-refundable); government bonds EUR 2,000,000 (minimum 2 years).
routes.processing_time: Nulla Osta 90 to 120 days; whole process 6 to 9 months
routes.family: Spouse, dependent children and dependent parents, with no extra investment.
routes.tax_note: Over 183 days a year in Italy makes you tax resident.
routes.name: Investor visa: innovative start-up
routes.summary: A 2-year permit for investing EUR 250,000 in an innovative start-up; the cheapest of Italy's four investor routes.
routes.requirements: Equity in a registered innovative start-up (under 5 years old, unlisted). Art. 26-bis of D.Lgs. 286/1998 and MIMIT decree of 21 July 2017. Thresholds cannot be combined across routes. Investment completed within 3 months of entry (one source). Held for the duration of the visa. Permit 2 years, renewals of 3 years.
routes.physical_presence: None required to keep the visa

routes.summary: Other investor routes: EUR 500,000 in an Italian company, EUR 1 million philanthropic donation, or EUR 2 million in government bonds.
routes.requirements: Same permit terms as the start-up route (2 years, then 3-year renewals). Company equity EUR 500,000; donation EUR 1,000,000 to a public-interest project in culture, education, immigration management, science or heritage (not refundable); bonds EUR 2,000,000 held at least 2 years.

routes.family: Each applicant may be asked to show funds; a couple is around EUR 37,000.
routes.tax_note: Over 183 days a year in Italy makes you tax resident on worldwide income; the EUR 200,000 new-resident flat tax is a separate election (not researched here).
routes.name: Elective residence visa
routes.summary: For people living on stable passive income who do not work in Italy; the income benchmark is set by consulates, about EUR 31,000 a year.
routes.requirements: No statutory figure. Sources quote EUR 31,000 to 32,000 a year for a single person and about EUR 37,000 to 38,000 for a couple (consular practice, varies by consulate). Pensions, rent, dividends and interest count; salary does not. Stable, documented income; Italian housing secured (not hotels or short lets); health insurance. No work, including remote work.

routes.fees_note: Visa application fee about EUR 116; permit-card fees not sourced.
routes.tax_note: Choose either the impatriate regime (50% exemption for 5 years, with a 4-year residence commitment) or the 5% flat tax regime for up to EUR 85,000 of revenue.
routes.name: Digital nomad and remote worker visa
routes.summary: For highly qualified remote workers earning about EUR 28,000 a year from non-Italian clients; consulates have accepted applications since March 2026.
routes.requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss national doing 'highly qualified' remote work (Blue Card standard: degree or 5 years of experience, at least 6 months of experience). Income about EUR 28,000 a year gross (the figure is linked to a health-exemption threshold and varies by consulate); spouse +EUR 9,900, each child +EUR 4,950. Health insurance of at least EUR 30,000, a registered 12-month lease, and about EUR 30,000 savings expected (one source). Implementing decree reported published 2 March 2026 with consulates accepting applications from 18 March 2026. Permit 1 year, renewable annually up to 5 years.
routes.physical_presence: No visa-specific minimum sourced; 183 days is needed for the impatriate tax regime

routes.summary: Non-EU workers are admitted through annual quotas (Decreto Flussi) with an employer's nulla osta; the Blue Card covers highly qualified staff.
routes.requirements: Employer-led, quota-based; details not researched in depth.
